chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Harun al-Fami (may God have mercy on him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Batta narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd from Musa ibn Umar ibn Bazee' who said:

I had two slave-wives who were pregnant, so I wrote to Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) informing him of this and asking him to supplicate to God that He make what is in their wombs two boys and grant me that. He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'I shall do so, if God wills.' Then he (peace be upon him) sent me a separate letter, its text being: 'In the Name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful. May God grant us and you the best of health in this world and the Hereafter with His Mercy! The affairs are in the hand of God, the Mighty and Exalted. He executes His decrees therein as He loves. A boy and a girl will be born to you, if God wills. Name the boy Muhammad and the girl Fatima, with the blessings of God, the Mighty and Exalted.' He said: 'So a boy and a girl were born to me exactly as he (peace be upon him) had said.'

key_terms.أَفْعَلُ: I shall do so (response to a request)
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Ridha (a title of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida)
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: In the Name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ar-Ridha (a.s.) predict about the children of Musa ibn Umar's pregnant slave-wives?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Imam’s divine foreknowledge (‘ilm al-ghayb) through a specific, verifiable prediction regarding the gender and names of the children, affirming his status as a sign of God’s leadership. The naming of the boy Muhammad and the girl Fatima underscores the enduring spiritual legacy of the Prophet’s household, linking the immediate miracle to the broader theological concept of the Ahl al-Bayt’s blessed lineage.
